Statement: Inculcate ‘Help ever-Hurt never’ in school going children at an early age. Assumptions: I. Any pain or wrong inflicted on another is but an affliction to oneself II. Good habits should be inculcated from childhood to grow up and become better people.
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the given statement and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

Inculcate ‘Help ever-Hurt never’ in school going children at an early age.

Assumptions:

I. Any pain or wrong inflicted on another is but an affliction to oneself

II. Good habits should be inculcated from childhood to grow up and become better people.

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are implicit
options.html: Both assumptions I and II are implicit

options.text: Either assumption I or II is implicit
options.html: Either assumption I or II is implicit

questions.solution:
Assumption I. Any pain or wrong inflicted on another is but an affliction to oneself

The statement doesn't say that its an affliction(pain) on self  in any way if any wrong is done with others. But it is implied that - "Hurt never" is said because of that in the Statement. So Assumption I doesn't directly follow but is implied.

II. Good habits should be inculcated from childhood to grow up and become better people.

The statement doesn't say anything about becoming better people. But its implied that if we teach "Help ever-Hurt never" in schools it guides them to be more considerate and thus become better people later in life. So Assumption II doesn't directly follow but is closely related and implied.

So Both I and II are implicit.

questions.question: During the Solung festival of the Adi tribe in Arunachal Pradesh, which traditional beverage is shared?
questions.questionHtml: During the Solung festival of the Adi tribe in Arunachal Pradesh, which traditional beverage is shared?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Apong.

Key Points

  • The Solung Festival is a major harvest festival celebrated by the Adi tribe, primarily in the state of Arunachal Pradesh, India.
  • During the festival, the traditional beverage called Apong is shared among the community members. Apong is a locally brewed rice beer that holds cultural and social significance for the Adi tribe.
  • The preparation of Apong involves fermenting rice along with other natural ingredients, which is a traditional method passed down through generations.
  • The sharing of Apong during the Solung festival symbolizes community bonding, joy, and gratitude for the harvest.
  • The Solung festival is not just about rituals; it also includes dances, songs, and the sharing of traditional food and beverages like Apong, making it a vibrant cultural event.

Additional Information

  • About the Solung Festival:
    • The Solung festival is celebrated annually by the Adi tribe in the month of September, though the exact date varies depending on the agricultural cycle.
    • The festival lasts for about five days and includes various rituals, including animal sacrifices and offerings to deities like Doying Bote, the goddess of prosperity.
    • It is a festival of thanksgiving to nature and a prayer for a good harvest, protection of crops, and the welfare of livestock.
  • Apong - The Traditional Beverage:
    • Apong is a traditional rice beer made using fermented rice and millet. It is an integral part of the Adi tribe’s cultural and social gatherings.
    • The process of making Apong is eco-friendly, as it utilizes bamboo containers and natural fermentation methods.
    • Apong is not only consumed during festivals but also during other social ceremonies like weddings and community feasts.
  • Other Options Explained:
    • Soma: Soma is a sacred drink mentioned in Vedic texts of ancient India, but it is not associated with the Adi tribe or the Solung festival.
    • Thukpa: Thukpa is a noodle soup that is popular in the Himalayan regions, especially among the Tibetan and Nepalese communities. It is not a traditional beverage.
    • Chhang: Chhang is a traditional alcoholic beverage of the Himalayan regions like Ladakh and Sikkim but is not part of the Solung festival celebrated by the Adi tribe.
  • Important Points:
    • The Adi tribe is one of the largest tribes in Arunachal Pradesh, known for their rich cultural traditions and agricultural lifestyle.
    • Festivals like Solung are crucial for preserving the cultural heritage and fostering unity within the community.
    • Apong, being an easily accessible and locally produced beverage, represents the self-sustaining lifestyle of the Adi tribe.

questions.question: Ghoomar dance was traditionally performed to worship which deity?
questions.questionHtml: Ghoomar dance was traditionally performed to worship which deity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Saraswati.

Key Points

  • Origin: Ghoomar dance originated among the Bhil tribe of Rajasthan.
  • Deity Worship: It was traditionally performed in worship of Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and learning.
  • Adoption: Later, the dance was adopted by Rajput communities, especially by women.
  • Occasions: Today, Ghoomar is performed during festivals like Gangaur, Teej, and on weddings and social ceremonies.

Additional Information

  • Lord Ganesha:
    • Lord Ganesha, also known as Ganapati or Vinayaka, is one of the most revered deities in Hinduism.
    • He is worshipped as the remover of obstacles, the patron of arts and sciences, and the deva of intellect and wisdom.
    • Ganesha's image is often depicted with an elephant head and a potbelly, symbolizing wisdom and prosperity.
    • Festivals such as Ganesh Chaturthi are dedicated to Lord Ganesha, where devotees celebrate his arrival and seek blessings for success and prosperity.
  • Other Deities in Indian Culture:
    • Shiva: Known as the destroyer and transformer in the Hindu triumvirate, Shiva is worshipped for spiritual growth and liberation.
    • Saraswati: The goddess of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and learning, she is worshipped during festivals like Vasant Panchami.
    • Krishna: An incarnation of Lord Vishnu, Krishna symbolizes love, compassion, and dharma. He is worshipped during Janmashtami.
  • Traditional Rajasthani Folk Dances:
    • Kalbelia: Performed by the Kalbelia community, this dance mimics the movements of snakes.
    • Chari Dance: Women perform this dance while balancing brass pots on their heads, often lit with fire inside.
    • Bhavai: A highly skilled dance, where dancers balance multiple pots on their heads while performing intricate movements.
  • Bollywood Representation:
    • Ghoomar was famously depicted in the Bollywood movie Padmaavat, showcasing the elegance and cultural richness of the dance.
    • Actress Deepika Padukone performed the Ghoomar dance in the film, bringing international attention to this traditional art form.

Important Points

  • Ghoomar Dance Origin:
    • Historically, Ghoomar was performed by women of the Rajput royalty to welcome brides into their new homes.
    • The dance symbolizes femininity, grace, and cultural pride, making it an integral part of Rajasthani traditions.
  • Modern-Day Popularity:
    • Ghoomar is now performed globally, representing Indian cultural heritage on international platforms.
    • The dance is often modified for stage performances, blending traditional movements with modern choreography.

The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Key Points

  • Assertion (A): The Chotanagpur Plateau forms an important part of the Peninsular Plateau of India. It is located mainly in Jharkhand and extends into parts of Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, and West Bengal. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
  • Reason (R): The Chotanagpur Plateau is indeed drained by the Damodar, Subarnarekha, North Koel, South Koel, and other rivers. Hence, Reason (R) is true.
  • However, the fact that the plateau is drained by the Damodar and Subarnarekha rivers does not explain why it forms part of the Peninsular Plateau.
  • The Chotanagpur Plateau is considered part of the Peninsular Plateau because it is composed of ancient crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks belonging to the Precambrian Age, which are characteristic features of the Peninsular Plateau region.
  • Therefore, both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Additional Information

  • Chotanagpur Plateau:
    • Known as the "Ruhr of India" due to its rich mineral resources.
    • Contains large deposits of coal, iron ore, mica, bauxite, copper, and limestone.
  • Peninsular Plateau:
    • It is the oldest and most stable landmass of India.
    • Composed mainly of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
    • Triangular in shape and surrounded by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
  • Damodar River:
    • Originates from the Chotanagpur Plateau in Jharkhand.
    • Historically known as the "Sorrow of Bengal" due to frequent floods.
  • Subarnarekha River:
    • Originates near Ranchi in Jharkhand.
    • Flows through Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal.
  • Economic Importance:
    • The plateau region hosts major industrial centers such as Jamshedpur, Bokaro, Dhanbad, and Ranchi.
    • It is one of India's most important mineral and industrial belts.

Important Points

  • The Peninsular Plateau is part of the ancient Gondwana Land.
  • The Chotanagpur Plateau is divided into the Ranchi Plateau, Hazaribagh Plateau, and Koderma Plateau.
  • The region is India's leading producer of several minerals, especially coal and iron ore.
  • The geological structure, not the drainage pattern, is the primary reason for its inclusion in the Peninsular Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about a Money Bill?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is correct about a Money Bill?

options.text: A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
options.html: A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the Speaker of Lok Sabha.

options.text: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a money bill.
options.html: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a money bill.

options.text: The Lok Sabha can either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
options.html: The Lok Sabha can either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: If there is a deadlock between the two Houses over the passage of a bill, the president can summon a joint sitting.
options.html: If there is a deadlock between the two Houses over the passage of a bill, the president can summon a joint sitting.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

  • A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the president.

Hence, option A is incorrect.

  • After it is passed by the Lok Sabha, it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its consideration.
  • The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a money bill. It can only make the recommendations.

Hence, option B is incorrect.

  • It must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, with or without recommendations.
  • The Lok Sabha can either accept/reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.

Hence, option C is correct.

  • If the Lok Sabha accepts any recommendation, the bill is then considered to have been passed by both the Houses
  • If the Lok Sabha does not accept any recommendation, the bill is then considered to be passed by both the Houses in the form originally approved by the Lok Sabha.
  • There is no provision of holding a joint sitting in case of disagreement between the two houses.

Hence, option D is incorrect.

  • If the Rajya Sabha fails to return the bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, the bill is deemed to have been accepted by both the Houses in the form originally approved by the Lok Sabha.

Consider the following statements about Article 270:

1) It deals with tax sharing between the Union and the States.

2) After the 101st Amendment, GST revenues were added under it.

3) Compensation Cess is also shared under Article 270.

Which statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Key Points

  • Statement 1: Article 270 deals with tax sharing between the Union and the States. It outlines the manner in which certain taxes collected by the Union are distributed between the Union and the States. This statement is correct.
  • Statement 2: After the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016), the Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced. GST revenues collected by the Union are now shared with the states under Article 270, as part of the tax-sharing mechanism. This statement is correct.
  • Statement 3: Compensation Cess is not shared under Article 270. The Compensation Cess is specifically collected to compensate states for revenue losses due to the implementation of GST and is governed by the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017. Therefore, it does not fall under Article 270. This statement is incorrect.
  • Hence, the correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Additional Information

  • Article 270 of the Indian Constitution:
    • Article 270 specifies the manner in which taxes are shared between the Union and the States.
    • Taxes such as Income Tax, Excise Duty, GST, and others collected by the Union are distributed among the states according to the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
    • The 101st Constitutional Amendment added provisions for sharing GST revenues between the Union and the States under Article 270.
  • GST and Tax Sharing:
    • The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in 2017 to replace multiple indirect taxes. It is shared between the Union and States, ensuring equitable revenue distribution.
    • Under the GST regime, states receive their share of taxes collected by the Union through Article 270.
  • Compensation Cess:
    • The Compensation Cess is collected under the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 and is used to compensate states for potential revenue losses due to GST implementation.
    • It is not included under Article 270 as it is meant solely for compensating states for losses, rather than tax-sharing.

Important Points

  • Finance Commission:
    • The Finance Commission recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and States under Article 270.
    • It ensures fairness in revenue distribution based on criteria such as population, income distance, and area.
  • 101st Constitutional Amendment:
    • Passed in 2016, this amendment introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST), a unified indirect tax regime replacing multiple taxes.
    • It modified Article 270 to include provisions for sharing GST revenues between the Union and States.

questions.question: The phenomenon caused by the falling of liquid in a thin tube is called _______.
questions.questionHtml: The phenomenon caused by the falling of liquid in a thin tube is called _______.
questions.solution: The phenomenon caused by the falling of liquid in a thin tube is called capillary action. Capillary action is the ability of a liquid to rise against gravity in a narrow tube or into a small space.

questions.question: A is 120% of B and B is 65% of C. If the sum of A, B and C is \(121 \frac{1}{2}\) , then the value of 2C – 4B + A is:
questions.questionHtml: A is 120% of B and B is 65% of C. If the sum of A, B and C is \(121 \frac{1}{2}\), then the value of 2C – 4B + A is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let C = 100 parts.

⇒ B = 65 parts and A = 120% of 65 = 78 parts.

⇒ Total Ratio = 78 + 65 + 100 = 243 parts.

⇒ Given Total = 121 1/2 = 243/2 ⇒ 1 part = 1/2.

⇒ Value to find = 2(100) − 4(65) + 78 = 200 − 260 + 78 = 18 parts.

⇒ Final Value = 18 × (1/2) = 9.

∴ The correct answer is 9.

Alternate Method

Given:

A is 120% of B

B is 65% of C

Sum of A, B, and C = 121 1/2 = 243/2

Calculations:

⇒ Let the value of C = 100x

⇒ B = 65% of 100x = 65x

⇒ A = 120% of 65x = (120/100) × 65x = 78x

⇒ A + B + C = 78x + 65x + 100x = 243x

⇒ Given, 243x = 243/2

⇒ x = (243/2) ÷ 243 = 1/2

We need to find the value of 2C − 4B + A:

⇒ 2(100x) − 4(65x) + 78x

⇒ 200x − 260x + 78x = 18x

Substitute the value of x:

⇒ 18 × (1/2) = 9

∴ The correct answer is 9.

Additional Information

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

Converting percentages to ratios simplifies calculations immensely. Example: 120% = 120/100 = 6/5. If A is 120% of B, the immediate ratio of A:B becomes 6:5.

Base Assumption in Successive Percentages

When multiple variables are linked successively (e.g., A depends on B, and B depends on C), assuming the final independent variable (C) as 100 or 100x effectively eliminates complex decimals and fractions.

Compound Ratio Method

To combine A:B = m:n and B:C = p:q into A:B:C, you can equate the common term (B) by finding the LCM of n and p, or use the direct pattern (m×p) : (n×p) : (n×q).

questions.question: A train running at 48 km/h takes 12 sec to pass a platform. Next it takes 8 sec to pass a man walking at 4 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going. Find the length of the platform.
questions.questionHtml: A train running at 48 km/h takes 12 sec to pass a platform. Next it takes 8 sec to pass a man walking at 4 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going. Find the length of the platform.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance covered (Train + Platform) = 48 × 5/18 × 12 = 160 m

Length of train (Lt) = Relative speed × time = (48 − 4) × 5/18 × 8 = 880/9 m

Length of platform (Lp) = Total distance − Lt = 160 − 880/9 = 560/9 m

Lp = 62.22 m ≈ 62.2 m

∴ The correct answer is 62.2 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of the train (St) = 48 km/h

Time taken to pass the platform (T1) = 12 sec

Speed of the walking man (Sm) = 4 km/h

Time taken to pass the man (T2) = 8 sec

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = St − Sm

Calculations:

⇒ Total distance covered to pass platform = Lt + Lp

⇒ Speed of train in m/s = 48 × 5/18 = 40/3 m/s

⇒ Lt + Lp = (40/3) × 12 = 160 m

⇒ Relative speed of train w.r.t the man = 48 − 4 = 44 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 44 × 5/18 = 110/9 m/s

⇒ Distance covered to pass the man = Length of the train (Lt)

⇒ Lt = (110/9) × 8 = 880/9 m

⇒ Substituting Lt in the first equation:

⇒ 880/9 + Lp = 160

⇒ Lp = 160 − 880/9

⇒ Lp = (1440 − 880) ÷ 9 = 560/9 m

⇒ Lp ≈ 62.2 m

∴ The correct answer is 62.2 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2). If moving in opposite directions, it is the sum (S1 + S2).

Train Crossing an Object

To cross a stationary object with no length (like a pole or standing man), the distance traveled is solely the length of the train. To cross an object with length (like a platform or bridge), the distance traveled is the length of the train plus the length of the object.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Three cubes of metal whose edges are in the ratio 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 are melted down into a single cube whose diagonal is \(12\sqrt 3 \) cm. Find the edges of the smallest cube.
questions.questionHtml: Three cubes of metal whose edges are in the ratio 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 are melted down into a single cube whose diagonal is \(12\sqrt 3 \) cm. Find the edges of the smallest cube.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The edges of the three cubes are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5.

Sum of their volumes ∝ 33 + 43 + 53 = 27 + 64 + 125 = 216 parts.

The edge of the newly formed single cube will be 3√216 = 6 parts.

Diagonal of the new cube = 6 parts × √3 = 12√3 cm ⇒ 1 part = 2 cm.

Edge of the smallest cube = 3 parts = 3 × 2 cm = 6 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of edges of three metal cubes = 3 : 4 : 5

Diagonal of the new single cube = 12√3 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a cube = a3

Diagonal of a cube = a√3

Calculations:

⇒ Let the edges of the three cubes be 3x, 4x, and 5x respectively.

⇒ Total volume of the three cubes = (3x)3 + (4x)3 + (5x)3

⇒ Total volume = 27x3 + 64x3 + 125x3 = 216x3

⇒ Let the edge of the newly formed single cube be A.

⇒ Volume of the new cube = A3 = 216x3

⇒ A = 3√(216x3) = 6x

⇒ Diagonal of the new cube = A√3 = 6x√3

⇒ Given diagonal = 12√3 cm

⇒ 6x√3 = 12√3

⇒ 6x = 12 ⇒ x = 2

⇒ Edge of the smallest cube = 3x = 3 × 2 = 6 cm

∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.

Additional Information

Volume Conservation

When one or more solid objects are melted to form a new shape, the total initial volume is perfectly conserved: Vnew = V1 + V2 + ... + Vn.

Important Cube Formulas

For a cube of side a: Volume = a3, Total Surface Area = 6a2, Lateral Surface Area = 4a2, and Body Diagonal = a√3.

Standard Triplets in Cubes

The numbers 3, 4, 5, and 6 form a special geometric triplet identity in cubes: 33 + 43 + 53 = 63. Recognizing this pattern significantly reduces calculation time in banking and standardized exams.

questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm a=\frac{1}{2+\sqrt3}\) and \(\rm b=\frac{1}{2-\sqrt3}\), then the value of a2b + ab2 =
questions.solution:
Given:

a = \(\rm \frac{1}{2+\sqrt3}\)

b = \(\rm \frac{1}{2-\sqrt3}\)

Formula used:

a2b + ab2 = ab(a + b)

(x + y)(x - y) = x2 - y2

Calculation:

a2b + ab2 = ab(a + b)

⇒ a = 2 - √3

⇒ b = 2 + √3

⇒ a + b = (2 - √3) + (2 + √3) = 4

⇒ ab = (2 - √3) × (2 + √3) = 4 - 3 = 1

⇒ a2b + ab2 = 1 × 4 = 4

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: The average age of a family of 6 members is 22 years. If the age of the youngest member is 7 years, what was the average age of the family just before the birth of the youngest member?
questions.questionHtml: The average age of a family of 6 members is 22 years. If the age of the youngest member is 7 years, what was the average age of the family just before the birth of the youngest member?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average age 7 years ago (treating 6 members) = 22 − 7 = 15 years.

Sum of their ages 7 years ago = 15 × 6 = 90 years.

Just before birth, the youngest is excluded, so family size was 5 members.

Required Average = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 years.

∴ The correct answer is 18 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of members in the family currently = 6

Current average age of the family = 22 years

Age of the youngest member = 7 years

Concept / Formula Used:

Sum of ages = Average × Number of members

Calculations:

⇒ Total age of the family currently = 6 × 22 = 132 years

⇒ When we go back 7 years, the age of each of the 6 members decreases by 7 years.

⇒ Total age 7 years ago = 132 − (6 × 7) = 132 − 42 = 90 years

⇒ Just before the birth of the youngest member, the family had only 5 members.

⇒ Average age of the family just before the birth = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 years

∴ The correct answer is 18 years.

Additional Information

Average of Age After/Before 'n' Years

If the average age of a constant group is A, then 'n' years later, the average becomes A + n, and 'n' years ago, it was A − n.

Replacement in Averages

When a person replaces another, the age of the new person = Age of removed person + (Net change in average × Total number of persons).

Combined / Weighted Average

Used when combining two groups with different averages. Combined Average = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: The incentre of Δ ABC with vertices A (1, √3), B (0, 0) and C (2, 0) is:
questions.questionHtml: The incentre of Δ ABC with vertices A (1, √3), B (0, 0) and C (2, 0) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Calculate side lengths using the distance formula: AB = 2, BC = 2, CA = 2.

Since all sides are equal, the given triangle is an equilateral triangle.

In an equilateral triangle, the Incentre is exactly the same as the Centroid.

Centroid (x, y) = [(x1 + x2 + x3) / 3, (y1 + y2 + y3) / 3]

Incentre = [(1 + 0 + 2) / 3, (√3 + 0 + 0) / 3] = (1, √3 / 3) = (1, 1/√3)

∴ The correct answer is (1, 1/√3).

Alternate Method

Given:

Vertices of ΔABC: A(1, √3), B(0, 0), and C(2, 0)

Formulas Used:

Distance Formula: d = √[(x2 − x1)2 + (y2 − y1)2]

Incentre Formula: I(x, y) = [(ax1 + bx2 + cx3) / (a + b + c) , (ay1 + by2 + cy3) / (a + b + c)]

⇒ a = BC = √[(2 − 0)2 + (0 − 0)2] = √4 = 2

⇒ b = AC = √[(1 − 2)2 + (√3 − 0)2] = √[(−1)2 + 3] = √4 = 2

⇒ c = AB = √[(1 − 0)2 + (√3 − 0)2] = √[1 + 3] = √4 = 2

⇒ Since a = b = c = 2, ΔABC is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ x-coordinate of I = (ax1 + bx2 + cx3) / (a + b + c)

⇒ x = (2 × 1 + 2 × 0 + 2 × 2) / (2 + 2 + 2) = (2 + 0 + 4) / 6 = 6 / 6 = 1

⇒ y-coordinate of I = (ay1 + by2 + cy3) / (a + b + c)

⇒ y = (2 × √3 + 2 × 0 + 2 × 0) / (2 + 2 + 2) = 2√3 / 6 = √3 / 3 = 1/√3

∴ The correct answer is (1, 1/√3).

Additional Information

Centroid of a Triangle

The point where all three medians intersect. It divides each median in a 2:1 ratio. Formula: G = [(x1+x2+x3)/3, (y1+y2+y3)/3].

Incentre of a Triangle

The point of intersection of the internal angle bisectors and the center of the incircle. Formula: I = [(ax1+bx2+cx3)/(a+b+c), (ay1+by2+cy3)/(a+b+c)].

Equilateral Triangle Centres

In a perfectly symmetrical equilateral triangle, all four major centres (Centroid, Incentre, Circumcentre, and Orthocentre) coincide at the exact same coordinate point.

questions.question: If x = 2 + √5 , then x 3 + 3x 2 - 29x :
questions.questionHtml: If x = 2 + √5 , then x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> - 29x :
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given x = 2 + √5 ⇒ x − 2 = √5

Squaring both sides: (x − 2)2 = 5 ⇒ x2 − 4x − 1 = 0

We need to evaluate x3 + 3x2 − 29x, which can be rewritten as (x + 7)(x2 − 4x − 1) + 7.

Substituting x2 − 4x − 1 = 0 into the expression gives: (x + 7)(0) + 7 = 7.

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Alternate Method

Given:

x = 2 + √5

Calculations:

⇒ x2 = (2 + √5)2 = 4 + 5 + 4√5 = 9 + 4√5

⇒ x3 = x × x2 = (2 + √5)(9 + 4√5)

⇒ x3 = 18 + 8√5 + 9√5 + 20 = 38 + 17√5

Substitute x, x2, and x3 into x3 + 3x2 − 29x:

⇒ (38 + 17√5) + 3(9 + 4√5) − 29(2 + √5)

⇒ 38 + 17√5 + 27 + 12√5 − 58 − 29√5

⇒ (38 + 27 − 58) + (17 + 12 − 29)√5

⇒ 65 − 58 + 0 = 7

∴ The correct answer is 7.

Additional Information

Surds and Radicals

When a root is given in the form a + √b, isolating the surd and squaring both sides eliminates the radical and provides a rational polynomial equation.

Polynomial Reduction

To evaluate a high-degree polynomial for a known quadratic root, divide the polynomial by the quadratic equation. The remainder equals the required value.

Algebraic Identities

The expansion formula (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 is used to square binomial surds efficiently during calculation.

questions.question: A fruit merchant makes a profit of 25% by selling mangoes at a certain price. If he charges Rs. 3 more on each mango, he will gain 40%. Find the cost price of one mango
questions.questionHtml: A fruit merchant makes a profit of 25% by selling mangoes at a certain price. If he charges Rs. 3 more on each mango, he will gain 40%. Find the cost price of one mango
questions.solution:
The difference in profit percentages corresponds to the Rs. 3 increase in selling price.

Thus, 1% corresponds to Rs. 3/15 = Rs. 0.20

Cost price (which is 100% of the price) = 100 × Rs. 0.20 = Rs. 20

questions.question: A salesman buys 15 articles for Rs. 10 and sells 10 articles for Rs. 15. Determine the percentage profit earned by the salesman.
questions.questionHtml: A salesman buys 15 articles for Rs. 10 and sells 10 articles for Rs. 15. Determine the percentage profit earned by the salesman.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Write Articles and Price side-by-side, then cross-multiply to find equivalent ratios:

CP ratio → Price (Buy) × Articles (Sell) = 10 × 10 = 100

SP ratio → Price (Sell) × Articles (Buy) = 15 × 15 = 225

Profit = 225 − 100 = 125

Profit % = (125 ÷ 100) × 100% = 125%

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost price of 15 articles = ₹10

Selling price of 10 articles = ₹15

Formula Used:

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100%

Calculations:

⇒ Let's equate the number of articles to simplify the calculation.

⇒ The LCM of 15 and 10 is 30.

⇒ CP of 30 articles = (10 ÷ 15) × 30 = ₹20

⇒ SP of 30 articles = (15 ÷ 10) × 30 = ₹45

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 45 − 20 = ₹25

⇒ Profit % = (25 ÷ 20) × 100%

⇒ Profit % = 1.25 × 100% = 125%

∴ The correct answer is 125%.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective discount is given by (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a trader claims to sell goods at CP but uses false weights, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100%.

questions.question: A man wants to purchase a car and for that, he checks the rating of the car on internet. He finds the ratings of \(\frac{9}{10}\) for comfort and \(\frac{8}{10}\) for resale value. Based on his requirements, he gives a weightage of 55% to comfort and 45% to resale value. Calculate the final rating of the car
questions.questionHtml: A man wants to purchase a car and for that, he checks the rating of the car on internet. He finds the ratings of \(\frac{9}{10}\) for comfort and \(\frac{8}{10}\) for resale value. Based on his requirements, he gives a weightage of 55% to comfort and 45% to resale value. Calculate the final rating of the car
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Directly apply the weighted average formula to the ratings:

Weighted Rating = (Comfort Rating × Comfort Weight) + (Resale Rating × Resale Weight)

⇒ Weighted Rating = (9 × 55% + 8 × 45%) / 10

⇒ Weighted Rating = (4.95 + 3.60) / 10 = 8.55 / 10

∴ The correct answer is 8.55/10.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rating for comfort = 9/10, Weightage = 55%

Rating for resale value = 8/10, Weightage = 45%

Formula Used:

Final Rating = (R1 × W1) + (R2 × W2)

Calculations:

⇒ Final Rating = (9/10 × 55/100) + (8/10 × 45/100)

⇒ Final Rating = (495/1000) + (360/1000)

⇒ Final Rating = (495 + 360) / 1000

⇒ Final Rating = 855 / 1000

⇒ Final Rating = 8.55 / 10

∴ The correct answer is 8.55/10.

Additional Information

Weighted Average

It is an average that takes into account the proportional relevance of each component. It is calculated by multiplying each value by its weight and then adding the results together. Formula: Aw = (w1x1 + w2x2) ÷ (w1 + w2).

Percentage Conversion

Percent literally means per hundred. To use a percentage in calculation, simply divide the percentage value by 100 (e.g., 55% = 55 ÷ 100 = 0.55).

questions.question: The perimeters of the two squares are respectively 40 cm and 32 cm. What is the perimeter of that third square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of two given squares?
questions.questionHtml: The perimeters of the two squares are respectively 40 cm and 32 cm. What is the perimeter of that third square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of two given squares?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sides of the two given squares are 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm and 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm.

Since the area of the third square is the difference of their areas, their sides form a Pythagorean triplet (6, 8, 10).

Thus, the side of the third square is directly found as 6 cm.

Perimeter of the third square = 4 × 6 = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of 1st square = 40 cm

Perimeter of 2nd square = 32 cm

Formula Used:

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

Area of a square = Side2

Calculation:

⇒ Side of 1st square = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm

⇒ Area of 1st square = 102 = 100 cm2

⇒ Side of 2nd square = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm

⇒ Area of 2nd square = 82 = 64 cm2

⇒ Area of 3rd square = Area of 1st square − Area of 2nd square

⇒ Area of 3rd square = 100 − 64 = 36 cm2

⇒ Side of 3rd square = √36 = 6 cm

⇒ Perimeter of 3rd square = 4 × 6

⇒ Perimeter of 3rd square = 24 cm

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal of a square with side 'a' is given by a√2. It divides the square into two congruent right-angled isosceles triangles.

Area using Diagonal

The area of a square can also be calculated directly from its diagonal (d) using the formula: Area = d2 ÷ 2.

Incircle and Circumcircle

For a square of side 'a', the radius of the incircle is a ÷ 2, and the radius of the circumcircle is a√2 ÷ 2.

questions.question: A student was getting the following four offers on the purchase of a book: I - Two successive discounts of 20% and 20% II - Two successive discounts of 25% and 15% III - Two successive discounts of 30% and 10% lV - Two successive discounts of 5% and 35% Which scheme offers the most discount to the student?
questions.questionHtml:
A student was getting the following four offers on the purchase of a book:

I - Two successive discounts of 20% and 20%

II - Two successive discounts of 25% and 15%

III - Two successive discounts of 30% and 10%

lV - Two successive discounts of 5% and 35%

Which scheme offers the most discount to the student?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the sum of two successive discounts is constant, the effective discount is maximized when their numerical difference is maximum.

The sum of the discounts in all four schemes is exactly 40%.

Difference for each scheme: I = 0%, II = 10%, III = 20%, IV = 30%.

Scheme IV has the maximum difference (35% − 5% = 30%), hence it provides the maximum effective discount.

∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.

Alternate Method

Given:

Four schemes of successive discounts on a book.

Formula Used:

Effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%

Calculations:

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme I = 20 + 20 − (20 × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme I = 40 − 4 = 36%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme II = 25 + 15 − (25 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme II = 40 − 3.75 = 36.25%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme III = 30 + 10 − (30 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme III = 40 − 3 = 37%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme IV = 35 + 5 − (35 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme IV = 40 − 1.75 = 38.25%

⇒ Comparing all the calculated effective discounts, 38.25% is the maximum overall discount.

∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are applied on a marked price, the net effective discount is given by the formula: (a + b − a×b÷100)%.

Maximizing Effective Discount

If the sum of multiple successive discounts is constant, the overall discount is highest when the product of the individual discounts is minimized. This occurs when their numerical difference is maximum.

Marked Price & Selling Price

A discount is always calculated over the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) after a discount of d% is evaluated as SP = MP × (100 − d)÷100.

Buy X Get Y Free

A widely used alternative discounting model. The effective discount percentage equals (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100.

questions.question: If a : b = 3 : 4, then what is the value of a 2 + b 2 : (a + b) 2 ?
questions.questionHtml: If a : b = 3 : 4, then what is the value of a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> : (a + b)<sup>2</sup> ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since both numerator and denominator of the required expression have the same degree (degree 2), substitute the ratio values directly.

Put a = 3 and b = 4 into a2 + b2 : (a + b)2

Numerator = 32 + 42 = 9 + 16 = 25

Denominator = (3 + 4)2 = 72 = 49

∴ The correct answer is 25 : 49.

Alternate Method

Given:

a : b = 3 : 4

Calculation:

⇒ Let a = 3x and b = 4x

⇒ Expression to evaluate: a2 + b2 : (a + b)2

⇒ Numerator = (3x)2 + (4x)2

⇒ Numerator = 9x2 + 16x2 = 25x2

⇒ Denominator = (3x + 4x)2

⇒ Denominator = (7x)2 = 49x2

⇒ Required Ratio = 25x2 : 49x2

⇒ Canceling the common factor x2, we get 25 : 49

∴ The correct answer is 25 : 49.

Additional Information

Homogeneous Expressions

When both the numerator and denominator of a fraction have the same total degree, direct substitution of ratio variables without a common constant (like x) provides the exact same result, saving time during exams.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of any given ratio a : b is determined by squaring both terms, which equals a2 : b2.

Componendo and Dividendo

If two ratios are equal such that a : b = c : d, then by the rule of componendo and dividendo, (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d).

questions.question: Which is the largest number which when divides 1553 and 2175 give respectively 3 and 5 as remainder?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the largest number which when divides 1553 and 2175 give respectively 3 and 5 as remainder?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Subtract the respective remainders to find the exactly divisible numbers.

Required number = HCF of (1553 − 3) and (2175 − 5) = HCF(1550, 2170)

The difference between 2170 and 1550 is 620, so the HCF must be a factor of 620.

Checking the given options, 310 is the largest factor of 620 that perfectly divides both 1550 and 2170.

∴ The correct answer is 310.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers to be divided = 1553 and 2175

Respective remainders = 3 and 5

Formula Used:

Largest dividing number = HCF of (First number − Remainder 1) and (Second number − Remainder 2)

Calculations:

⇒ First perfectly divisible number = 1553 − 3 = 1550

⇒ Second perfectly divisible number = 2175 − 5 = 2170

⇒ Now, we determine the HCF of 1550 and 2170 using prime factorization.

⇒ 1550 = 2 × 5 × 5 × 31 = 2 × 52 × 31

⇒ 2170 = 2 × 5 × 7 × 31

⇒ The common prime factors are 2, 5, and 31.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 5 × 31 = 310

∴ The correct answer is 310.

Additional Information

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The highest common factor of two or more numbers is the largest possible number that divides each of them completely without leaving any remainder.

LCM (Lowest Common Multiple)

The lowest common multiple is the smallest positive integer that is a perfectly divisible multiple of two or more given numbers.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF with Same Remainder

To find the largest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, calculate the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

questions.question: A 21 m high flag post is cut in such a way that its top touches the ground and makes an angle of 30° with the ground. At what height form the bottom is the post cut?
questions.questionHtml: A 21 m high flag post is cut in such a way that its top touches the ground and makes an angle of 30° with the ground. At what height form the bottom is the post cut?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the opposite sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The perpendicular (height of the remaining post) corresponds to 1 part.

The hypotenuse (broken part of the post) corresponds to 2 parts.

Total height of the flag post = 1 part + 2 parts = 3 parts.

3 parts = 21 m ⇒ 1 part = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 m.

∴ The correct answer is 7 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total height of the flag post = 21 m

Angle of elevation made by the broken part with the ground = 30°

Formula Used:

sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

Calculations:

Let the height from the bottom where the post is cut be x m.

Length of the broken top part that forms the hypotenuse = (21 − x) m.

In the right-angled triangle formed,

⇒ sin(30°) = x ÷ (21 − x)

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = x ÷ (21 − x)

⇒ 21 − x = 2x

⇒ 3x = 21

⇒ x = 7 m

∴ The correct answer is 7 m.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratio of 30°-60°-90° Triangle

The sides opposite to the angles 30°, 60°, and 90° in a right-angled triangle are always in the standard ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line of sight, whereas the angle of depression is measured downwards. In alternate interior configurations, these two angles are equal.

Basic Trigonometric Properties

sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos(θ) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse | tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

questions.question: If x + y + z = 1, x 2 + y 2 + z 2 = 2 and x 3 + y 3 + z 3 = 3, then what is the value of xyz?
questions.questionHtml: If x + y + z = 1, x2 + y2 + z2 = 2 and x3 + y3 + z3 = 3, then what is the value of xyz?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for (xy + yz + zx) = [(x + y + z)2 − (x2 + y2 + z2)] ÷ 2 = (1 − 2) ÷ 2 = −1/2

Now apply the main cubic identity: x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)[x2 + y2 + z2 − (xy + yz + zx)]

⇒ 3 − 3xyz = 1 × [2 − (−1/2)]

⇒ 3 − 3xyz = 5/2

⇒ 3xyz = 3 − 5/2 = 1/2 ⇒ xyz = 1/6

∴ The correct answer is 1/6.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + y + z = 1

x2 + y2 + z2 = 2

x3 + y3 + z3 = 3

Formula Used:

(x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)[x2 + y2 + z2 − (xy + yz + zx)]

Calculations:

⇒ (1)2 = 2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ 1 − 2 = 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ 2(xy + yz + zx) = −1

⇒ (xy + yz + zx) = −1/2

Substitute the values into the cubic formula:

⇒ 3 − 3xyz = 1 × [2 − (−1/2)]

⇒ 3 − 3xyz = 2 + 1/2

⇒ 3 − 3xyz = 5/2

⇒ 3xyz = 3 − 5/2

⇒ 3xyz = 1/2

⇒ xyz = 1/6

∴ The correct answer is 1/6.

Additional Information

Special Case for Cubic Identity

If x + y + z = 0, then the cubic identity simplifies directly to x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz.

Alternate Cubic Formula

x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = 1/2 × (x + y + z) × [(x − y)2 + (y − z)2 + (z − x)2]

Algebraic Identity for Squares

(x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

questions.question: In a bag the ratio of red balls to green balls is 4 ∶ 9. If 6 more green balls were added to the bag, the ratio of red balls to green balls would become 1 ∶ 3. How many red balls are there in the bag?
questions.questionHtml: In a bag the ratio of red balls to green balls is 4 ∶ 9. If 6 more green balls were added to the bag, the ratio of red balls to green balls would become 1 ∶ 3. How many red balls are there in the bag?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since only green balls are added, the number of red balls remains unchanged. We make the red ratio parts equal.

Initial Ratio (Red : Green) = 4 : 9

Final Ratio (Red : Green) = 1 : 3 → Multiply by 4 → 4 : 12

Increase in Green parts = 12 − 9 = 3 parts.

3 parts = 6 balls ⇒ 1 part = 2 balls.

∴ The correct answer is 8 balls.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial ratio of red balls to green balls = 4 : 9

Number of green balls added = 6

Final ratio of red balls to green balls = 1 : 3

Calculations:

Let the number of red balls be 4x and green balls be 9x.

After adding 6 green balls, the new number of green balls = 9x + 6

⇒ 4x / (9x + 6) = 1 / 3

By cross multiplying:

⇒ 3 × 4x = 1 × (9x + 6)

⇒ 12x = 9x + 6

⇒ 12x − 9x = 6

⇒ 3x = 6

⇒ x = 2

Number of red balls = 4x

⇒ 4 × 2 = 8 balls

∴ The correct answer is 8 balls.

Additional Information

Equivalent Ratios

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same non-zero number does not change its value. For example, a : b = (a × k) : (b × k).

Proportion

When two ratios are equal (a : b = c : d), they are in proportion. The product of extremes equals the product of means (a × d = b × c).

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a : b and c : d is defined as the product of their respective antecedents and consequents, given by ac : bd.

questions.question: The dimensions of a cuboid are proportional to 5 : 3 : 4. The total surface area of the cuboid is 846 cm 2 . Volume of this cuboid is -
questions.questionHtml: The dimensions of a cuboid are proportional to 5 : 3 : 4. The total surface area of the cuboid is 846 cm<sup>2</sup>. Volume of this cuboid is -

options.html: 540 cm3
1620 cm3
4860 cm3

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Surface area ratio parts = 2(5 × 3 + 3 × 4 + 4 × 5) = 94 parts

94 parts = 846 ⇒ 1 squared part = 846 ÷ 94 = 9

1 linear part = √9 = 3

Volume parts = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cubic parts

Volume = 60 × (3)3 = 60 × 27 = 1620 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 1620 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Dimensions of the cuboid are proportional to 5 : 3 : 4

Total Surface Area = 846 cm2

Formula Used:

Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Volume of Cuboid = l × b × h

Calculations:

Let length (l) = 5x, breadth (b) = 3x, and height (h) = 4x.

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2[(5x × 3x) + (3x × 4x) + (4x × 5x)]

⇒ 846 = 2[15x2 + 12x2 + 20x2]

⇒ 846 = 2[47x2]

⇒ 94x2 = 846

⇒ x2 = 846 ÷ 94

⇒ x2 = 9

⇒ x = √9 = 3

Now, Volume = 5x × 3x × 4x

⇒ Volume = 60x3

⇒ Volume = 60 × (3)3

⇒ Volume = 60 × 27 = 1620 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 1620 cm3.

Additional Information

Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid

The total area of the four vertical side faces, calculated by the formula 2h(l + b).

Length of Diagonal of Cuboid

The longest distance connecting two opposite inside corners, given by √(l2 + b2 + h2).

Total Surface Area of Cube

For a perfect cube with side length 'a', the Total Surface Area is equal to 6a2.

Volume of Cube

For a regular cube with identical side length 'a', the Volume is calculated as a3.

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 42 km/h. For how many minute does the bus stop per hour?
questions.questionHtml: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 42 km/h. For how many minute does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for stoppage time per hour:

Stoppage time = [(Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed] × 60 minutes

Stoppage time = [(60 − 42) ÷ 60] × 60

Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed without stoppages = 60 km/h

Speed with stoppages = 42 km/h

Formula Used:

Stoppage time per hour = Distance not covered due to stoppages ÷ Speed without stoppages

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 60 km

⇒ Distance actually covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 42 km

⇒ Loss in distance due to stoppage = 60 − 42 = 18 km

⇒ Time required to cover this 18 km at the normal speed of 60 km/h represents the total stoppage time.

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Stoppage time = 18 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ To convert into minutes, multiply by 60.

⇒ Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.

Additional Information

Average Speed with Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, including both driving time and the time the vehicle was stationary.

Average Speed without Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the actual driving time only, completely ignoring any stopping periods.

Direct Formula for Stoppage Time

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster speed − Slower speed) ÷ Faster speed. To get the time in minutes, simply multiply the fraction by 60.

questions.question: One-third of a natural number is 56 more than one-fifth of 125. Find the square root of the required natural number.
questions.questionHtml: One-third of a natural number is 56 more than one-fifth of 125. Find the square root of the required natural number.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

One-fifth of 125 = 125 ÷ 5 = 25

One-third of the required number = 25 + 56 = 81

The required natural number = 81 × 3 = 243

Square root of the number = √243 = 9√3

∴ The correct answer is 9√3.

Alternate Method

Given:

One-third of a natural number is 56 more than one-fifth of 125.

Method Used:

Form a linear equation and simplify using basic arithmetic operations to find the unknown value, then calculate its square root.

Calculations:

Let the required natural number be x.

⇒ x / 3 = (125 / 5) + 56

⇒ x / 3 = 25 + 56

⇒ x / 3 = 81

⇒ x = 81 × 3

⇒ x = 243

We need to find the square root of the required natural number:

⇒ √x = √243

⇒ √x = √(81 × 3)

⇒ √x = 9√3

∴ The correct answer is 9√3.

Additional Information

BODMAS Rule

Used to solve arithmetic expressions in the order of Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Surds Simplification

To simplify a square root, separate the number into a perfect square and another factor: √(a2 × b) = a√b.

Linear Equations

An algebraic equation where the highest power of the variable is 1. It is solved by performing inverse operations to isolate the variable.

questions.question: The marked price of a folding bed is ₹18,000. Aman bought it after two successive discount of 15% and 10%. He spent ₹830 on transportation and sold it for ₹18,440. Find his profit.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a folding bed is ₹18,000. Aman bought it after two successive discount of 15% and 10%. He spent ₹830 on transportation and sold it for ₹18,440. Find his profit.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive discount multiplying factor = (1 − 0.15) × (1 − 0.10) = 0.85 × 0.9 = 0.765

Buying price before transport = 18000 × 0.765 = ₹13,770

Total CP = 13770 + 830 (Transportation) = ₹14,600

Profit = SP − Total CP = 18440 − 14600 = ₹3,840

∴ The correct answer is ₹3,840.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹18,000

Successive discounts = 15% and 10%

Transportation cost = ₹830

Selling Price (SP) = ₹18,440

Formula Used:

Selling price after successive discounts = MP × (1 − D1/100) × (1 − D2/100)

Total CP = Buying Price + Overhead expenses

Profit = SP − Total CP

Calculations:

⇒ Price of the bed after discounts = 18000 × (1 − 15/100) × (1 − 10/100)

⇒ Price = 18000 × (85/100) × (90/100)

⇒ Price = 18000 × 0.85 × 0.9 = ₹13,770

⇒ Total CP for Aman = 13770 + 830 = ₹14,600

⇒ Profit earned = SP − Total CP

⇒ Profit = 18440 − 14600 = ₹3,840

∴ The correct answer is ₹3,840.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

When two discounts D1% and D2% are given consecutively, the effective equivalent discount is given by (D1 + D2 − D1×D2/100)%.

Overhead Expenses

Any additional money spent on transportation, repairs, or maintenance is always added to the base buying price to determine the actual total Cost Price (CP).

Profit and Loss Baseline

Both Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the total Cost Price unless specifically mentioned otherwise in the question context.

Key Points
  • The Buddha and Nagarjuna both challenge the limits of language and concepts, especially regarding ultimate reality and the state of the enlightened after death, suggesting some truths are ineffable and cannot be captured by conventional categories.
    • This is the main idea of the passage. The text begins by explaining that the Buddha refused to answer questions about the afterlife of an enlightened person, hinting that conventional logical frameworks (like the catuskoti) don't apply.
    • It then details how Nagarjuna expanded on this, arguing that while language frames our "conventional reality," the "ultimate reality" beneath it is entirely ineffable (indescribable) and can only be experienced, not defined by the four possibilities of the catuskoti.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Additional Information

  • Option 2: Incorrect because the final paragraph notes that ultimate reality "can be experienced directly in certain meditative states," validating meditation rather than rejecting it.
  • Option 3: Incorrect because Nagarjuna is described as "probably the most important and influential Buddhist philosopher," and his work deals with profound philosophical concepts like "emptiness" (sunya) and ultimate reality, not scientific logic.

The author openly invites reflection, noting that things will get "disconcerting" and explicitly leaving the task of making precise logical sense of these claims "for the reader to ponder."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Additional Information

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • While arranging the parts of the passage given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let’s find out.  
    • The first statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.
    • It should be a continuation or extension of S1.
    • Q follows S1 because it is talking about Young Lincoln's way of keeping shop.
    • S follows Q because it is adding more details about  Young Lincoln's way of keeping shop.
    • P follows S because it is talking about the arrival of a customer.
    • R is directly connected to S6 as it is talking about reading which is mentioned in S6.
    • S6 provides a conclusion to the story.
  • Therefore, the sequence is 'S1QSPRS6.'
  • Thus, the correct answer is 'QSPR.'
  • ​​The correct sequence:

questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Susan Reynolds slipped into her car after putting her shopping bags in the trunk.

B. She reached her house and carried the shopping bags in.

C. It was a thirty-minute ride to her home and the traffic was light.

D. She put them down and turned off the alarm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ACBD'.

Key Points    

  • Statement A will come first as it contains the subject i.e. 'Susan Reynolds' and the context of the paragraph.
  • Statement C will follow statement A as it tells what she did next after putting her bags in the trunk of her car.
  • Statement B will follow statement C as it mentions that she has reached her house for which she was driving in statement C.
  • Statement D will come last.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

The final sequence will be: 

  • A: Susan Reynolds slipped into her car after putting her shopping bags in the trunk.
  • C: It was a thirty-minute ride to her home and the traffic was light.
  • B: She reached her house and carried the shopping bags in.
  • D: She put them down and turned off the alarm.

Key Points

  • Correlative conjunctions: They work together and relate one sentence element to another.
  • Correlative conjunctions include pairs such as “both/and,” “either/or,” “neither/nor,” “not/but” and “not only/but also.”
    • Example: We’ll have both the cheesecake and the chocolate cake.
  • Therefore, the given sentence is correct because correct correlative conjunction pair (not only/but also) is used.
